description: Blocks and APIs that impose structure on a Simulink model: subsystems that group blocks, conditionally executed subsystems driven by enable, trigger, function-call, if and switch-case control, iterator and For Each subsystems, and the reuse mechanisms (referenced models, referenced subsystems, variants, masks). It also covers the user-defined function blocks that embed MATLAB code, System objects, Simulink functions and external C into a diagram.

tools.name: Subsystem
tools.description: Groups a set of blocks into a single block, creating one level of model hierarchy. By default a Subsystem is virtual: it is flattened at compile time and exists only for readability. Setting Treat as atomic unit makes it a real execution unit that runs as a single indivisible step, which is what enables sample-time specification, code reuse as a function, and most conditional-execution options. Use subsystems to name and encapsulate a function of the design, and make them atomic when you need deterministic execution order or reusable generated code.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Subsystem', [mdl '/Ctrl'])

parameters.name: TreatAsAtomicUnit
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. 'on' makes the subsystem atomic so it executes as a unit and can have its own sample time and code-generation function.

parameters.name: SystemSampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time of an atomic subsystem; '-1' inherits from the contained blocks.

parameters.name: RTWSystemCode
parameters.description: Code-generation packaging: 'Auto', 'Inline', 'Nonreusable function' or 'Reusable function'. Requires Simulink Coder.

parameters.name: RTWFcnNameOpts
parameters.description: 'Auto', 'Use subsystem name' or 'User specified' - how the generated function is named.

parameters.name: RTWFcnName
parameters.description: Explicit generated function name when RTWFcnNameOpts is 'User specified'.

parameters.name: ReferencedSubsystem
parameters.description: File name of a subsystem file, which turns the block into a Subsystem Reference.

parameters.name: ShowPortLabels
parameters.description: 'FromPortIcon', 'FromPortBlockName', 'SignalName' or 'none'.

parameters.name: Permissions
parameters.description: 'ReadWrite', 'ReadOnly' or 'NoReadOrWrite' - protects the contents from editing or viewing.

parameters.name: PermitHierarchicalResolution
parameters.description: 'All', 'ExplicitOnly' or 'None' - how variable names inside resolve against parent workspaces.

tools.notes: An Atomic Subsystem ('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Atomic Subsystem') is the same block with TreatAsAtomicUnit preset to 'on'. Making a subsystem atomic can introduce algebraic loops where a virtual one had none. Use Simulink.BlockDiagram.createSubsystem to wrap existing blocks, and Simulink.SubSystem.convertToModelReference to promote one to a referenced model.

tools.name: Enabled Subsystem
tools.description: A subsystem that executes only while the signal feeding its Enable port is positive, and holds or resets its outputs and states otherwise. It is the block-diagram equivalent of running a piece of an algorithm only under a condition that persists over time, such as a controller that runs only when a system is armed. The Enable block inside decides whether states are held or reset when the subsystem is re-enabled.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Enabled Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Enabled Subsystem', [mdl '/EnaSub'])

parameters.name: StatesWhenEnabling
parameters.description: On the contained Enable block: 'held' keeps the states from the last execution, 'reset' returns them to their initial values.

parameters.name: ShowOutputPort
parameters.description: On the Enable block: 'on' exposes the enable value as a signal inside the subsystem.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: On the Enable block: 'on' | 'off'. Zero-crossing detection so a variable-step solver lands exactly on the enable transition.

parameters.name: PropagateVarSize
parameters.description: On the Enable block: when variable-size signals may change dimensions - 'Only when enabling' or 'During execution'.

parameters.name: OutputWhenDisabled
parameters.description: On each contained Out1 block: 'held' or 'reset' - what the port emits while the subsystem is disabled.

tools.notes: An Enable port can be added to any subsystem by dropping 'simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Enable' inside it; the preconfigured block is just a convenience. Combine with Merge when several mutually exclusive enabled subsystems drive one signal. An Enabled and Triggered Subsystem requires both conditions to be satisfied at the same step.

tools.name: Triggered Subsystem
tools.description: A subsystem that executes exactly once each time the signal at its Trigger port produces a qualifying edge - rising, falling or either. Between triggers its outputs hold their last values. Use it for event-driven logic such as sampling on a hardware interrupt, latching a value on a button press, or running a computation once per detected zero crossing. A triggered subsystem inherits a triggered sample time, so it cannot contain continuous-time blocks.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Triggered Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Triggered Subsystem', [mdl '/TrigSub'])

parameters.name: TriggerType
parameters.description: On the contained Trigger block: 'rising', 'falling', 'either', 'function-call' or 'message'.

parameters.name: ShowOutputPort
parameters.description: On the Trigger block: 'on' exposes the trigger value (1, -1 or 0) as a signal inside the subsystem.

parameters.name: OutputDataType
parameters.description: On the Trigger block: data type of that trigger-value output, for example 'auto' or 'int8'.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: On the Trigger block: 'on' | 'off' for zero-crossing detection on the trigger signal.

parameters.name: StatesWhenEnabling
parameters.description: On a function-call Trigger block: 'held', 'reset' or 'inherit' behaviour for contained states.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Triggered Subsystem', [mdl '/TrigSub']);
set_param([mdl '/TrigSub/Trigger'], 'TriggerType', 'rising', 'ShowOutputPort', 'on');
tools.notes: Blocks inside a triggered subsystem must all support an inherited (triggered) sample time - Integrator and other continuous blocks are rejected. Use Unit Delay or Memory inside to build latches. For a subsystem that must be both armed and edge-driven use Enabled and Triggered Subsystem.

tools.name: Function-Call Subsystem
tools.description: A subsystem executed on demand when another block issues a function-call event on its control port - typically a Stateflow chart, a Function-Call Generator, an S-Function or an interrupt-service block. Unlike a triggered subsystem it can be called several times within a single time step and the caller controls the exact execution point. Use it to model interrupt handlers, scheduler-driven tasks and export-function components where the calling environment owns the timing.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Function-Call Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Function-Call Subsystem', [mdl '/FcnSub'])

parameters.name: TriggerType
parameters.description: On the contained Trigger block: set to 'function-call' for this subsystem type.

parameters.name: StatesWhenEnabling
parameters.description: On the Trigger block: 'held', 'reset' or 'inherit' - what happens to contained states between calls.

parameters.name: SampleTimeType
parameters.description: On the Trigger block: 'triggered' (executes only when called) or 'periodic' (the caller guarantees a fixed period, which allows continuous states and discrete rates inside).

parameters.name: TreatAsAtomicUnit
parameters.description: Always 'on' for a function-call subsystem; it executes as an indivisible unit.

tools.notes: Use the Function-Call Generator block to drive one periodically, and Function-Call Split ('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Function-Call Split') to fan one call signal out to several subsystems with a defined execution order. A function-call subsystem whose SampleTimeType is 'triggered' cannot contain continuous-time blocks. Export-function models are built entirely from function-call subsystems at the root level.

tools.name: Resettable Subsystem
tools.description: A subsystem that runs on every time step like an ordinary atomic subsystem, but whose internal states are reset to their initial values whenever the signal at its Reset port produces a qualifying edge. It separates the notions of 'execute' and 'reinitialise', which an Enabled Subsystem conflates. Use it for integrators, counters and filters that must be zeroed on a mode change or fault recovery without pausing the rest of the computation.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Resettable Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Resettable Subsystem', [mdl '/RstSub'])

parameters.name: ResetTriggerType
parameters.description: On the contained Reset block: 'rising', 'falling', 'either' or 'level hold' - the edge that causes the reset.

parameters.name: PropagateVarSize
parameters.description: On the Reset block: when variable-size signals may change dimensions.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: On the Reset block: 'on' | 'off' for zero-crossing detection on the reset signal.

parameters.name: TreatAsAtomicUnit
parameters.description: Always 'on' - a resettable subsystem is atomic by construction.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Resettable Subsystem', [mdl '/RstSub']);
set_param([mdl '/RstSub/Reset'], 'ResetTriggerType', 'rising', 'ZeroCross', 'on');
tools.notes: A Reset port can be added to any subsystem by placing 'simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Reset' inside it. Only blocks with resettable states are affected; blocks that hold no state are unchanged. For finer-grained reinitialisation of individual states use an Initialize/Reset/Terminate Function block with a State Writer.

tools.name: If
tools.description: Evaluates an if / elseif / else chain over its inputs and emits an action signal on exactly one output port. The conditions are written as MATLAB-style expressions in terms of u1, u2, ... referring to the block's input ports. It does not compute anything itself - each output must drive an If Action Subsystem that holds the branch body. Use it when only one branch of a computation should actually execute, unlike a Switch where every branch runs.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > If  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/If', [mdl '/If'])

parameters.name: NumInputs
parameters.description: Number of input ports available to the condition expressions as u1, u2, ...

parameters.name: IfExpression
parameters.description: The if condition, for example 'u1 > 0'.

parameters.name: ElseIfExpressions
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of elseif conditions, for example 'u1 < -1, u2 == 0'. Each adds one output port.

parameters.name: ShowElse
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Adds a final else output port that fires when no condition matched.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Zero-crossing detection on the condition transitions.

tools.notes: Condition expressions may only use the input ports, comparison and logical operators and constants - no workspace variables and no function calls. Merge the outputs of the driven If Action Subsystems with a Merge block. For dispatch on an integer value use the Switch Case block instead.

tools.name: If Action Subsystem
tools.description: A subsystem whose execution is controlled by an Action port driven from one output of an If block, so it runs only when that branch is selected. It is a preconfigured Subsystem containing an Action Port block plus In1/Out1. Use one per branch of an if/elseif/else structure, and feed their outputs into a Merge block so downstream logic sees a single continuously defined signal.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > If Action Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/If Action Subsystem', [mdl '/ThenBranch'])

parameters.name: InitializeStates
parameters.description: On the contained Action Port block: 'held', 'reset' or 'inherit' - what happens to contained states when the branch is not selected.

parameters.name: PropagateVarSize
parameters.description: On the Action Port block: how variable-size signals are propagated.

parameters.name: OutputWhenDisabled
parameters.description: On each contained Out1 block: 'held' or 'reset' - the value emitted while this branch is not active.

tools.notes: The first input port of an Action Subsystem is the action (control) port, so ordinary data inports start at index 2 when wiring with add_line. Switch Case Action Subsystem is the equivalent block for Switch Case branches - the two are interchangeable in structure but must be driven from the matching controller.

tools.name: Switch Case
tools.description: Dispatches to one of several action outputs based on an integer-valued input, the diagram form of a C switch statement. Each case is a value or a list of values in braces, and an optional default port handles anything unmatched. Use it for mode logic and state dispatch where the number of branches makes an If chain unwieldy; each output drives a Switch Case Action Subsystem holding that branch's body.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Switch Case  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Switch Case', [mdl '/Case'])

parameters.name: CaseConditions
parameters.description: Cell array of case values, for example '{1, [2 3], 4}'. Each entry creates one output port and may list several values.

parameters.name: ShowDefaultCase
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Adds a default output port used when no case matches.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Zero-crossing detection on the case-selection input.

tools.notes: The control input is truncated to an integer, so a floating-point mode signal should be converted deliberately with a Data Type Conversion block first. Without a default port an unmatched value simply runs no branch, leaving the merged output at its held value - usually you want ShowDefaultCase 'on'.

tools.name: For Iterator Subsystem
tools.description: Repeats its contents a fixed or signal-determined number of times within a single simulation time step, like a C for loop. The contained For Iterator block sets the iteration count, exposes the current index, and decides whether internal states persist between time steps. Use it for sequential algorithms that must run to completion inside one step, such as iterative solvers, search loops or per-element processing of a vector with feedback between elements.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > For Iterator Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/For Iterator Subsystem', [mdl '/ForSub'])

parameters.name: IterationSource
parameters.description: On the contained For Iterator block: 'internal' (count from the dialog) or 'external' (count supplied on an input port).

parameters.name: IterationLimit
parameters.description: Number of iterations when IterationSource is 'internal'.

parameters.name: ResetStates
parameters.description: 'held' or 'reset' - whether internal states persist from one time step to the next.

parameters.name: ShowIterationPort
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Outputs the current iteration index for use inside the loop.

parameters.name: IndexMode
parameters.description: 'Zero-based' or 'One-based' iteration index.

parameters.name: ExternalIncrement
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Shows a Next_i port so the loop body can compute the next index itself.

parameters.name: IterationVariableDataType
parameters.description: Data type of the iteration-index output, for example 'int32' or 'double'.

tools.notes: Every iteration happens at the same simulation time, so continuous blocks are not allowed inside. If the iterations are independent, a For Each Subsystem is usually faster and generates better code. Use Assignment and Selector blocks with the iteration index to read and write vector elements inside the loop.

tools.name: For Each Subsystem
tools.description: Applies the same algorithm independently to each slice of one or more array inputs and concatenates the results back into an array output. Unlike a For Iterator Subsystem each repetition has its own copy of the internal states, so the block models N independent instances of a component rather than N steps of one loop. Use it for per-channel filters, per-wheel controllers or any vectorised component where the instances do not interact.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > For Each Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/For Each Subsystem', [mdl '/EachSub'])

parameters.name: InputPartition
parameters.description: On the contained For Each block: 'on' | 'off' per input port - whether that input is sliced or broadcast whole to every iteration.

parameters.name: PartitionDimension
parameters.description: Dimension along which each partitioned input is sliced.

parameters.name: PartitionWidth
parameters.description: Width of each slice taken from the input.

parameters.name: PartitionOffset
parameters.description: Offset of the first slice within the input.

parameters.name: OutputConcatenation
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off' per output port - whether the per-iteration results are concatenated into an array.

parameters.name: ConcatenationDimension
parameters.description: Dimension along which the outputs are concatenated.

parameters.name: StatesPartitioning
parameters.description: Whether each iteration gets its own copy of the internal states.

parameters.name: SpecifiedNumIters
parameters.description: Explicit number of iterations, when it is not implied by the input partitioning.

tools.notes: Because states are replicated per iteration, a For Each Subsystem containing a Unit Delay gives each channel its own delay memory - exactly what a per-channel filter needs. Parameters can also be partitioned, so each instance can use a different gain. Code generation emits a single reusable function called in a loop, which keeps generated code small.

tools.name: While Iterator Subsystem
tools.description: Repeats its contents within a single time step for as long as a logical condition input remains true, up to a maximum iteration count. The contained While Iterator block chooses between while semantics (test before executing) and do-while semantics (execute then test). Use it for convergence loops such as a Newton iteration or a search that must finish inside one step, and always set a finite MaxIters so a non-converging model cannot hang the simulation.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > While Iterator Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/While Iterator Subsystem', [mdl '/WhileSub'])

parameters.name: WhileBlockType
parameters.description: On the contained While Iterator block: 'while' (condition and an initial-condition IC port) or 'do-while' (body runs at least once, no IC port).

parameters.name: MaxIters
parameters.description: Maximum iterations allowed in one time step; '-1' means unlimited (not recommended).

parameters.name: ResetStates
parameters.description: 'held' or 'reset' - whether internal states persist between time steps.

parameters.name: ShowIterationPort
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Outputs the number of iterations executed.

parameters.name: OutputDataType
parameters.description: Data type of the iteration-count output, for example 'int32'.

tools.notes: In 'while' mode the subsystem gains an IC port that decides whether the first iteration runs at all. Continuous blocks are not allowed inside because all iterations share one simulation time. Hitting MaxIters is reported by the 'While loop maximum iterations exceeded' diagnostic.

tools.name: Model
tools.description: References another Simulink model as a component, giving true file-level modularity: the referenced model is compiled and simulated separately, with a fixed interface and its own configuration. Instance parameters let several Model blocks reference the same model with different parameter values. Use model reference (rather than subsystems) for large designs, team development, incremental build, protected models and unit testing of components in isolation.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Model  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Model', [mdl '/Plant'])

parameters.name: ModelNameDialog
parameters.description: Name of the referenced model, with or without the file extension. 'ModelName' (no extension) and 'ModelFile' (with extension) are also accepted.

parameters.name: SimulationMode
parameters.description: 'Normal', 'Accelerator', 'Software-in-the-loop (SIL)' or 'Processor-in-the-loop (PIL)'.

parameters.name: InstanceParameters
parameters.description: Struct array with fields Name, Value, Path and Argument giving per-instance values for the referenced model's parameter arguments.

parameters.name: ParameterArgumentNames
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of the referenced model's model arguments.

parameters.name: ParameterArgumentValues
parameters.description: Query-only parameter returning the current argument values for this instance.

tools.notes: A referenced model has a fixed interface: data types, dimensions and sample times at its root ports must be fully specified, unlike a subsystem which adapts to context. Use Simulink.SubSystem.convertToModelReference to promote an existing subsystem, Simulink.ModelReference.protect to ship a model without exposing its contents, and Simulink.ModelReference.refresh to pick up interface changes.

tools.name: Variant Subsystem
tools.description: A container holding several alternative implementations of the same function, exactly one of which is active in any given simulation or build. Each child (Subsystem, Model block or Subsystem Reference) is associated with a variant control condition, and the activation time decides whether the choice is fixed at update-diagram, at code compile time via #if, or at model startup. Use it to manage product lines, hardware options and plant-model fidelity levels in a single model.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Variant Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Variant Subsystem', [mdl '/Plant'])

parameters.name: VariantControlMode
parameters.description: 'expression' (conditions are MATLAB expressions over workspace variables), 'label' (choose a choice by name), 'sim codegen switching' or 'expression (codegen switching)'.

parameters.name: VariantControls
parameters.description: Mapping of variant control conditions to the child blocks that implement each choice.

parameters.name: VariantActivationTime
parameters.description: 'update diagram', 'update diagram analyze all choices', 'code compile' or 'startup' - when the active choice is resolved.

parameters.name: LabelModeActiveChoice
parameters.description: Name of the active choice when VariantControlMode is 'label'.

parameters.name: VariantControlVariable
parameters.description: The variable whose value selects the choice in the newer variant-control workflows.

parameters.name: PropagateVariantConditions
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Propagates variant conditions into the surrounding diagram so inactive regions are removed too.

parameters.name: AllowFlexibleInterface
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Lets the choices have different port counts, with the Variant Subsystem interface adapting.

parameters.name: EmptyChoice
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Allows a configuration where no choice is active.

tools.notes: With 'expression' mode the control conditions are evaluated in the base workspace or a data dictionary, commonly using Simulink.VariantControl or Simulink.Variant objects. Choosing 'code compile' activation keeps every choice in the generated code behind preprocessor conditionals. Variant Source and Variant Sink apply the same idea at signal level; a Model block configured with variant choices is referred to as a Variant Model.

tools.name: Variant Source
tools.description: Selects one of several input signal paths according to variant conditions, removing the inactive branches from the compiled model entirely rather than just ignoring them. Because inactive paths are pruned, blocks feeding them are eliminated from simulation and from generated code. Use it for signal-level variation - swapping a sensor model for a stub, or switching between simulation-only and code-generation sources - where a full Variant Subsystem would be heavy.
tools.usage: Simulink > Signal Routing > Variant Source  |  add_block('simulink/Signal Routing/Variant Source', [mdl '/VSrc'])

parameters.name: VariantControlMode
parameters.description: 'expression', 'label' or 'sim codegen switching'.

parameters.name: VariantControls
parameters.description: The variant conditions associated with each input port.

parameters.name: VariantActivationTime
parameters.description: 'update diagram', 'update diagram analyze all choices', 'code compile' or 'startup'.

parameters.name: LabelModeActiveChoice
parameters.description: Active choice name when VariantControlMode is 'label'.

parameters.name: AllowZeroVariantControls
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Permits a configuration where no input condition is true.

parameters.name: ShowConditionOnBlock
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Annotates each port with its variant condition.

parameters.name: OutputFunctionCall
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Allows the block to route function-call signals.

tools.notes: Variant Source with 'sim codegen switching' is the supported replacement for the Environment Controller block, which was removed from the Signal Routing library in R2021b. Variant Sink is the mirror image, selecting which of several downstream paths receives a signal. Unlike a Switch, the unselected branches cost nothing at run time.

tools.name: Subsystem Reference
tools.description: References a subsystem stored in its own .slx file, so one definition can be instantiated many times across models and edited in a single place. Unlike model reference, a referenced subsystem keeps the flexible interface of an ordinary subsystem - the same file can be instantiated with scalar inputs in one place and vectors in another - and it is not separately compiled. Use it for reusable building blocks that need context adaptation but should not be duplicated by copy and paste.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Subsystem Reference  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Subsystem Reference', [mdl '/Filter'])

parameters.name: ReferencedSubsystem
parameters.description: Name of the subsystem file (.slx or .mdl) this block instantiates. Setting it on an ordinary Subsystem block turns that block into a subsystem reference.

parameters.name: ShowPortLabels
parameters.description: 'FromPortIcon', 'FromPortBlockName', 'SignalName' or 'none'.

parameters.name: TreatAsAtomicUnit
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. A referenced subsystem may be virtual or atomic just like an inline one.

tools.notes: Subsystem reference was introduced in R2019b. It gives incremental loading and reduces merge conflicts compared with copying subsystems, but unlike model reference it offers no separate compilation, no SIL/PIL and no fixed interface contract. Use the Simulink Editor's Convert command, or set ReferencedSubsystem on an existing Subsystem block, to convert an inline subsystem into a referenced one.

tools.name: MATLAB Function
tools.description: Embeds a MATLAB function directly in the model, compiled to C for simulation and code generation. It supports the code-generation subset of the MATLAB language, including control flow, structures, enumerations, fixed-point types and persistent variables for state. Use it for algorithms that are far easier to express in code than in blocks - table interpolation logic, state machines with heavy arithmetic, string or struct manipulation - while keeping the result fully code-generatable.
tools.usage: Simulink > User-Defined Functions > MATLAB Function  |  add_block('simulink/User-Defined Functions/MATLAB Function', [mdl '/Algo'])

parameters.name: Script (via the Stateflow API)
parameters.description: The function body. Set it with the EMChart object's Script property: rt = sfroot; ch = rt.find('-isa','Stateflow.EMChart','Path',blkPath); ch.Script = code.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Block sample time; '-1' inherits from the driving signals.

parameters.name: UpdateMethod
parameters.description: 'Inherited', 'Discrete' or 'Continuous' execution of the function.

parameters.name: SupportVariableSizing
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Allows variable-size inputs and outputs.

tools.notes: The block's input and output ports are derived from the function signature, so editing the Script changes the port count - re-wire after a scripted update. Only the code-generation subset of MATLAB is allowed; calls to unsupported functions must be wrapped in coder.extrinsic (simulation only). Use persistent variables for state and declare them with the standard 'if isempty(x)' initialisation pattern. Interpreted MATLAB Function runs arbitrary MATLAB but cannot be code-generated.

tools.name: MATLAB System
tools.description: Brings a MATLAB System object (a class derived from matlab.System) into a Simulink model, giving a structured, object-oriented way to implement a block with setup, step, reset and release phases. The System object's properties become block dialog parameters, and its stepImpl method provides the algorithm. Use it when an algorithm has significant internal state or initialisation, when you want the same implementation to run in MATLAB and Simulink, or to reuse System objects from DSP, Communications and Computer Vision toolboxes.
tools.usage: Simulink > User-Defined Functions > MATLAB System  |  add_block('simulink/User-Defined Functions/MATLAB System', [mdl '/Sys'])

parameters.name: System
parameters.description: Fully qualified class name of the System object, for example 'myPkg.MyFilter'.

parameters.name: SimulateUsing
parameters.description: 'Code generation' (compiled, faster, restricted to the code-generation subset) or 'Interpreted execution' (runs the MATLAB code directly).

parameters.name: SaturateOnIntegerOverflow
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Integer overflow behaviour for fixed-point operations inside the object.

parameters.name: ShowFiSettings
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Exposes the fixed-point settings section of the dialog.

tools.notes: Implement getNumInputsImpl / getNumOutputsImpl, getOutputSizeImpl, getOutputDataTypeImpl and isOutputFixedSizeImpl in the class so Simulink can resolve the interface without running the object. Use matlab.system.mixin.Propagates for non-trivial propagation. The class file must be on the MATLAB path when the model compiles.

tools.name: Simulink Function
tools.description: Defines a reusable function inside a Simulink model that can be invoked by Function Caller blocks, Stateflow charts or MATLAB Function blocks, rather than by a wired signal connection. The body is an ordinary subsystem whose interface is described by a Trigger block in function-call mode plus Argument Inport and Argument Outport blocks. Use it for service-oriented designs - a shared arbitration routine, a diagnostic service, a message handler - where several clients need the same operation without duplicating the blocks.
tools.usage: Simulink > User-Defined Functions > Simulink Function  |  add_block('simulink/User-Defined Functions/Simulink Function', [mdl '/computeLimit'])

parameters.name: Function name (on the contained Trigger block)
parameters.description: The name clients call; also shown in the function prototype text on the block icon.

parameters.name: Function visibility (on the Trigger block)
parameters.description: 'scoped' (visible within the model hierarchy), 'global' (visible to every model) or 'port' (exposed through a function-call port).

parameters.name: ShowPortLabels
parameters.description: 'FromPortIcon', 'FromPortBlockName', 'SignalName' or 'none'.

parameters.name: PermitHierarchicalResolution
parameters.description: 'All', 'ExplicitOnly' or 'None' - how variables inside resolve against parent workspaces.

parameters.name: Permissions
parameters.description: 'ReadWrite', 'ReadOnly' or 'NoReadOrWrite'.

tools.notes: The prototype is stored on the block icon rather than as a simple set_param parameter; the function name and visibility live on the Trigger block inside. A Simulink Function placed at the root of a model and made global can be called from any model in the hierarchy. Related: Function Caller (the client block), Initialize/Reset/Terminate Function blocks (event-driven variants) and Message Triggered Subsystem for message-driven services.

tools.name: Function Caller
tools.description: Calls a Simulink Function, an exported Stateflow graphical function or a function defined in another model, passing arguments in and receiving results out. The prototype string defines the call syntax, and the argument specifications pin down data types and dimensions when they cannot be inherited. Use it wherever a client needs a shared service, which decouples callers from the implementation and avoids duplicating the same blocks in several places.
tools.usage: Simulink > User-Defined Functions > Function Caller  |  add_block('simulink/User-Defined Functions/Function Caller', [mdl '/callLimit'])

parameters.name: FunctionPrototype
parameters.description: The call syntax, for example 'y = computeLimit(u)' or '[a,b] = f(u1,u2)'. This determines the block's ports.

parameters.name: ScopedFunctionName
parameters.description: Qualified name shown on the icon when the target is scoped, for example 'Client.f'.

parameters.name: InputArgumentSpecifications
parameters.description: Comma-separated type/size specifications for the inputs, for example 'single(1)' or 'int16([2 3])'.

parameters.name: OutputArgumentSpecifications
parameters.description: Comma-separated type/size specifications for the outputs.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Interval between calls; '-1' inherits.

parameters.name: AsynchronousCaller
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Marks the call as asynchronous with respect to the caller's rate.

tools.notes: The prototype must match the target Simulink Function exactly, including argument order and count, or the model fails to compile. Argument specifications are required when the function lives in a different model and the types cannot be propagated. A single Simulink Function may have many Function Caller clients; calls execute in the caller's task.

tools.name: C Caller
tools.description: Calls a function from external C source code directly, with Simulink generating the port interface automatically from the C prototype. You register the source files and headers in the model's Simulation Target settings, then pick a function from the discovered list. Use it to reuse validated legacy C algorithms, driver code or third-party libraries inside a model without hand-writing an S-function.
tools.usage: Simulink > User-Defined Functions > C Caller  |  add_block('simulink/User-Defined Functions/C Caller', [mdl '/callC'])

parameters.name: FunctionName
parameters.description: Name of the C function to call, chosen from the functions discovered in the registered source files.

parameters.name: AvailableFunctions
parameters.description: Read-only cell array of the C functions Simulink found in the custom code settings.

parameters.name: FunctionPortSpecification
parameters.description: Object describing how each C argument maps to a Simulink port (input, output, parameter, scope and label).

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Interval between calls in seconds; '-1' inherits.

tools.notes: Only C constructs Simulink can map to signals are supported - pointer-heavy or void* interfaces usually need a wrapper function. The C Function block ('simulink/User-Defined Functions/C Function', parameters OutputCode, StartCode, InitializeConditionsCode, TerminateCode) is the more flexible relative: it lets you write the glue code inline and call several functions per block. Legacy Code Tool and S-Function Builder remain available for more complex integrations.

tools.name: Simulink.Mask
tools.description: The programmatic interface to block masks: the custom dialog, icon and parameter set that turns a subsystem into a self-documenting, reusable component. Create a mask on a block, add typed parameters that map to variables used by the blocks inside, write initialisation code, and draw an icon - all from a script. Use it to build a library of parameterised components without hand-editing dialogs, and to regenerate masks reproducibly as part of a model-build script.
tools.usage:
maskObj = Simulink.Mask.create(blockPath)
maskObj = Simulink.Mask.get(blockPath)
p = maskObj.addParameter('Type', 'edit', 'Name', 'K', 'Prompt', 'Gain', 'Value', '1')
maskObj.delete()

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Mask type string, shown in the dialog title and returned by get_param(blk,'MaskType').

parameters.name: Description
parameters.description: Descriptive text shown at the top of the mask dialog.

parameters.name: Display
parameters.description: MATLAB drawing commands that render the block icon, for example "disp('Gain K')" or a plot command.

parameters.name: Initialization
parameters.description: MATLAB code executed when the mask is loaded or a parameter changes; typically used to compute derived values.

parameters.name: Parameters
parameters.description: Array of Simulink.MaskParameter objects; managed with addParameter, getParameter, insertParameter and removeParameter.

parameters.name: IconOpaque
parameters.description: 'opaque', 'transparent' or 'opaque-with-ports' - how the icon hides the contained blocks.

parameters.name: ParameterConstraints
parameters.description: Validation rules added with addParameterConstraint and addCrossParameterConstraint.

tools.notes: Mask parameter names become variables in the block's mask workspace, so blocks inside the subsystem can simply reference Kp and Ki in their expressions. Simulink.Mask.get returns an empty array if the block has no mask - check before calling methods on it. Related parameters on the block itself: MaskType, MaskPromptString, MaskValues and MaskEnables, which the older get_param/set_param mask interface uses.

tools.name: Simulink.BlockDiagram.createSubsystem
tools.description: Wraps a set of existing blocks into a new Subsystem block in place, automatically adding Inport and Outport blocks for every signal that crossed the boundary and reconnecting the surrounding lines. Called with no arguments it operates on the current selection in the editor. Use it to refactor a flat diagram into a hierarchy from a script, which is far more reliable than adding a subsystem and moving blocks by hand.
tools.usage:
Simulink.BlockDiagram.createSubsystem(blocks)
Simulink.BlockDiagram.createSubsystem()
Simulink.BlockDiagram.createSubsystem(___, 'Name', name, 'MakeNameUnique', 'on'|'off')

parameters.name: blocks
parameters.description: Vector of block handles to group. All blocks must be at the same level of the same model.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Name for the new subsystem block.

parameters.name: MakeNameUnique
parameters.description: 'on' (default) appends a number if the name is taken; 'off' errors instead.

tools.notes: Pass block handles, not path strings - use get_param(...,'Handle'). The function errors if the selection spans hierarchy levels or includes blocks that cannot be grouped, such as root-level Inports in some configurations. The resulting subsystem is virtual; set TreatAsAtomicUnit afterwards if you need atomic behaviour.

tools.name: Simulink.SubSystem.convertToModelReference
tools.description: Converts one or more Subsystem blocks into separate referenced models, creating the new model files and replacing each subsystem with a Model block that points at them. It runs a set of compatibility checks first and reports anything that blocks the conversion, such as unresolved interface attributes or goto/from tags crossing the boundary. Use it to promote a subsystem to a true component once it is stable enough to deserve its own file, test harness and build.
tools.usage: success = Simulink.SubSystem.convertToModelReference(subsystem, modelName, 'Name', Value)

parameters.name: subsystem
parameters.description: Path, handle, or cell array of paths of the Subsystem blocks to convert.

parameters.name: modelName
parameters.description: Name (or cell array of names) for the referenced models to create.

parameters.name: AutoFix
parameters.description: true | false. Automatically fixes issues it can, such as moving required data into the new model's workspace.

parameters.name: ReplaceSubsystem
parameters.description: true | false. Replaces the original subsystem with a Model block instead of only creating the file.

parameters.name: BuildTarget
parameters.description: 'Sim' or 'RTW' - whether to check compatibility for simulation or for code generation.

parameters.name: CheckSimulationResults
parameters.description: true | false. Compares simulation results before and after conversion to confirm equivalence.

parameters.name: Force
parameters.description: true | false. Proceeds despite warnings from the compatibility checks.

tools.notes: The subsystem must be atomic and have a fully determined interface - referenced models cannot inherit sample times or data types the way subsystems can. Data stores, goto tags and mask parameters that cross the boundary are the usual causes of failure; AutoFix handles many but not all. The Model Reference Conversion Advisor is the interactive equivalent.

tools.name: libinfo
tools.description: Returns a struct array describing every library-linked block in a model or subsystem: where the instance sits, which library it came from, the path of the source block and the state of the link. Use it to audit which library versions a model depends on, to find blocks whose links have been disabled or broken, and as the input to a script that restores or removes links in bulk.
tools.usage:
libdata = libinfo(modelName)
libdata = libinfo(modelName, 'BlockType', 'SubSystem')

parameters.name: modelName
parameters.description: Model, subsystem path or handle to search.

parameters.name: Block
parameters.description: Returned field: path of the linked block instance inside the model.

parameters.name: Library
parameters.description: Returned field: name of the source library.

parameters.name: ReferenceBlock
parameters.description: Returned field: path of the block within its source library.

parameters.name: LinkStatus
parameters.description: Returned field and a settable block parameter: 'none' (no link / fully disconnected), 'resolved', 'unresolved', 'implicit', 'inactive' (disabled link) or 'restore'.

tools.notes: Setting LinkStatus to 'none' is irreversible - the instance becomes a plain copy and stops tracking library updates, so prefer 'inactive' while experimenting. A block reported as 'unresolved' means its library is missing from the MATLAB path. Use find_system(mdl,'LookUnderMasks','all','FollowLinks','on',...) when you need to search inside linked blocks.
